shortDescription: Polish inflation accelerated more than expected in August due to fuel prices, raising the likelihood that interest rates will remain unchanged through year-end.

children: Polish inflation accelerated more than expected in August due to fuel prices, raising the likelihood that interest rates will remain unchanged through year-end.
Inflation (PLCFY=ECI), (PLCFM=ECI) rose to 3.4% year-on-year, while analysts expected a 3.1% increase. The month-on-month price growth rate was 0.4% versus an estimated 0.2%.
CPI accelerated mainly due to the increase in fuel prices - 24.2% year-on-year and 5.2% month-on-month, which was a result of the government ending the fuel price control program.
Although the government cut VAT rates on petrol and diesel in the second half of August, the move failed to fully offset higher global commodity prices.
Analysts expect inflation to continue rising in the coming months and it may reach around 4.0% by the end of 2026, reducing the scope for monetary easing by the National Bank of Poland.
"There will be no interest rate cuts in September or until the end of the year," Pekao Bank analysts wrote in a note following the data release.
The meeting of the Monetary Policy Council (MPC) will be held on September 8 to 9.
Separate data published on Monday confirmed that the economy continued to expand at a solid pace in the second quarter.

Gross domestic product grew 3.9% year-on-year in the second quarter, slightly above the previously reported 3.8%, and analysts point to a significant acceleration in investments, which increased by 8.4% compared to 2.4% in the first quarter.
"The economy is resilient to conflict in the Middle East in the second quarter of 2026," ING analysts said.
